newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares sit tight amid currency jitters.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares sit tight amid currency jitters.

text.p: Singapore share prices held in tight ranges at noon Friday amid a fresh round of currency jitters in the region after the Philippines' effective devaluation of its currency.
The 30-share Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) trickled down 2.73 points to 1,965.61 at the midday break after being tied to a narrow 1962.72-1968.50 band.
"In the past two days, funds had been selling on talk of a peso devaluation. After the (Philippine) announcement today, funds are just not comfortable with the region," a broker said.
"After Thailand, Philippines, there's talk the same could happen to Malaysia although it's very unlikely," she said.
The Philippines Central Bank said early on Friday it was allowing the peso to trade in a wider band against the dollar, just over a week after Thailand's move to a managed float of the baht.

Malaysian over-the-counter (OTC) stocks attempted a technical rebound but slipped again as Kuala Lumpur stocks remained under pressure after Bank Negara's recent strong stand on defending the ringgit.
The OTC index eased 2.79 points to 1,097.09.
The market was also in a lull as it waited for the budget to be unveiled from 0800 GMT, dealers said.
"Property stocks are seeing some rebound and electronic stocks are steady," said another dealer.
The property index gained 5.21 points to 680.44 led by a Singapore $0.12 bounce in DBS Land to S$4.66 on 1.87 million shares.
"The market is just sideways. The emotion is like the budget in that people don't think anything will happen but of course we wish the market will pull up," a dealer said.
Total volume was light at 69.3 million shares with gainers ahead of losers by 157 to 114.
